correctness.rationale: Central character idempotent for a finite group has constant matrix row/column absolute sum d E|chi|. For Steinberg d=q^(n(n−1)/2), the standard character theorem vanishes off semisimple elements and assigns |St(s)|=|C_G(s)|_p on semisimple classes. Rational canonical semisimple centralizers GL_m(F_{q^d}) give class weights 1/prod_{i<=m}(q^(di)−1). Expanding Euler products over irreducible monic polynomials with nonzero constant term yields Z_q(u)=(1−u)^(−1)prod_{r>=1}(1−u²q^(−(2r−1)))/(1−u²q^(−2r)). The q-binomial theorem gives A_n=sum_{j<=floor(n/2)} a_j with a_1=−1/(q+1) and ratio (q^(2j−2)−q)/(q^(2j)−1); later ratios in (0,q^(−2)). This proves two-rank plateaus, strictly decreasing even ranks, positive Euler limit and geometric tail. Independent exact rational canonical-type sums match recurrence in all 36 (q,n) cases q in {2,3,4,5}, n=0..8. Finite checks only corroborate the reconstructed all-rank proof; exhaustive small GL matrix/flag enumeration in bundled verify.py was inspected but not rerun this turn.
